status.en: 132 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 132 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen have repeatedly attacked former football star Segun Odegbami at his home in Abeokuta, wounding him but he survived the machete assault by three armed men. Security personnel have been targeted, including a university guard shot dead in Plateau and another guard ambushed and killed while returning home with his wife. A mining site in Plateau was attacked, resulting in three feared dead, and a herder was shot dead in Plateau. Police operations in Benue rescued kidnapped victims and neutralised suspected bandits. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Skytevåpnede menn har gjentatte ganger angrepet den tidligere fotballstjernen Segun Odegbami i hans hjem i Abeokuta, såret ham, men han overlevde macheteangrepet fra tre bevæpnede menn. Sikkerhetspersonell har blitt målrettet, inkludert en universitetsvakt som ble skutt og drept i Plateau og en annen vakt som ble overfalt og drept mens han var på vei hjem med sin kone. Et gruveområde i Plateau ble angrepet, noe som førte til tre savnede, og en hyrde ble skutt og drept i Plateau. Politioperasjoner i Benue reddet bortførte personer og nøytraliserte mistenkte banditter. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
